title: Microcommitments playbook for top-account SLA concessions and roadmap acceptance
creator: Lena Park
description: Create an operational playbook that formalizes negotiated microcommitments (timeboxed, minimal-scope deliverables) for top accounts and escalations. The playbook will provide a repeatable intake, scoring, negotiation, and acceptance flow so PMs, Sales, and Eng can agree faster on committed scope with clear rollback/fallback rules.
background: Over the last 4 quarters we have been informally promising narrow feature changes to strategic accounts to preserve renewals. Those ad-hoc commitments create downstream churn, block engineering prioritization, and lead to SLA/expectation mismatches. We need a lightweight, verifiable mechanism to convert customer asks into short, well-scoped deliverables (microcommitments) with measurable acceptance criteria and replayable negotiation logic.
goals: 1) Reduce ambiguous scope commitments for top accounts by 80% within 2 cycles. 2) Shorten time-to-decision on escalated roadmap asks to <= 5 business days. 3) Produce a standard microcommitment artifact that includes acceptance tests, rollback triggers, and a capacity cost estimate.
scope: In scope: intake templates, scoring rubric, negotiation guidelines, standard microcommitment artifact, implementation runbook for PM/SE/Sales, and basic console tagging for committed items. Out of scope: full contract/legal templates, pricing negotiation playbook, and enterprise procurement workflows.
proposed_process: 1) Intake: Sales/CS open a microcommitment request via the intake form (Drive template) with required signals and urgency. 2) Triage: PM on-call evaluates using the scoring rubric within 48 hours. 3) Negotiation: PM + Eng TL + Sales craft microcommitment (max 4 sprint-days work, timeboxed 30 days). 4) Acceptance: Customer signs off on acceptance tests; we add tag 'microcommitment:<id>' in the roadmap. 5) Delivery & verification: Engineering delivers, QA runs acceptance tests, customer acceptance recorded and contract note added.
scoring_rubric: Signals used: renewal risk, ARR at stake, feature reach (affected customers), reliability/regulatory severity, operational risk (SLO breaches). Score buckets: 0-4 (low) => backlog lane, 5-7 (medium) => discretionary sprint lane, 8-10 (high) => microcommitment lane with escalation. Each signal is given a 0-2 weight; rubric spreadsheet linked in links.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form template published and linked in Sales playbook

Percentage of top-account commitments using microcommitment artifact (target 75% Q2)
Number of post-delivery renegotiations per microcommitment (target <= 10%)
Delta in roadmap churn measured as number of ad-hoc scope inserts per quarter (target -50%)
